newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu, Arafat open Hebron summit.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu, Arafat open Hebron summit.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat opened a summit on the Israel-Gaza border on Tuesday in a bid to clinch a long-elusive deal on Hebron, witnesses said.

The two men last met at an emergency summit in Washington called by U.S. President Bill Clinton in the aftermath of fierce clashes between Israeli and Palestinian security forces that killed 75 last September.
Before the meeting opened, U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross dampened expectations a deal on an Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town could be sealed on Tuesday.

"We have clearly energised negotiations over the last couple of days," Ross told reporters, in a reference to his mediation shuttle that began late on Saturday. But he added: "I don't expect that one meeting is going to conclude this."
Israel and the PLO have accused each other of foot-dragging in nearly three months of talks on Hebron, most of which was due to have been handed over to Palestinian self-rule last March.
